hints: Note that because the ring is smooth, the tension $T$ is uniform throughout both parts of the string ($AR$ and $BR$).
Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium: $T\sin 30^\circ + T\sin 40^\circ = 2\text{ N}$.
Resolve forces vertically: $T\cos 30^\circ - T\cos 40^\circ = mg$, and substitute $T$ to find mass $m \approx 0.0175\text{ kg}$.
walkthrough: Note that because the ring is smooth, the tension $T$ is identical throughout the string.

Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium ($\Sigma F_x = 0$):
$$T\sin 30^\circ + T\sin 40^\circ = 2$$
$$T(\sin 30^\circ + \sin 40^\circ) = 2$$
$$T(0.5 + 0.6428) = 2 \implies 1.1428 T = 2$$
$$T = \frac{2}{1.1428} \approx 1.75\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium ($\Sigma F_y = 0$):
$$T\cos 30^\circ - T\cos 40^\circ - mg = 0$$
$$mg = T(\cos 30^\circ - \cos 40^\circ)$$
$$10m = 1.7501(0.8660 - 0.7660) = 1.7501(0.09998) \approx 0.1750$$
$$m = \frac{0.1750}{10} = 0.0175\text{ kg}$$

ai_rubric.Applying Coplanar Equilibrium: Resolves horizontally to get T(sin 30 + sin 40) = 2 giving T = 1.75 N, vertically to get T(cos 30 - cos 40) = mg giving m = 0.0175 kg.

teacher_walkthrough: State the physical principle for a smooth ring: because the string is continuous and runs freely through the smooth ring, the tension $T$ is identical in both sections $AR$ and $BR$.

Resolve forces horizontally (taking the direction of the $2\text{ N}$ horizontal pull as positive):
$$2 - T\sin 30^\circ - T\sin 40^\circ = 0$$
$$T(\sin 30^\circ + \sin 40^\circ) = 2$$

Divide 2 by 1.142788 to find $T$:
$$T = \frac{2}{1.142788} \approx 1.75006\text{ N}$$
$$T = 1.75\text{ N}\quad (\text{to 3 significant figures})$$

Resolve forces vertically (taking upwards as positive):
$$T\cos 30^\circ - T\cos 40^\circ - mg = 0$$
$$mg = T(\cos 30^\circ - \cos 40^\circ)$$

Substitute $T = 1.75006\text{ N}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$10m = (1.75006)(0.099981) \approx 0.174973$$
$$m = \frac{0.174973}{10} \approx 0.017497\text{ kg}$$
$$m = 0.0175\text{ kg}\quad (\text{to 3 significant figures})$$
